title: Four uses of delta: sensitivity, probability, share equivalent, hedge ratio
summary: Delta has four uses. One: price sensitivity, a 50 delta option moves 50 cents per $1 move in the stock. Two: a rough probability of finishing in the money, so a 20 delta call has about a 20% chance. Three: share equivalent, one 60 delta call acts like 60 shares. Four: hedge ratio, sell 60 shares against that call to be delta neutral, for example before earnings.

steps.caption: The stock trades at $100. We hold one call with the $97 strike, about 60 delta.
The strike. At the money, delta is near 50.
Use one: price sensitivity. A 50 delta option moves about 50 cents for each $1 in the stock.
Use two: rough probability. A 20 delta call has about a 20% chance of finishing in the money.
Use three: share equivalent. One 60 delta call acts like 60 shares, since one contract is 100 shares.
Use four: hedge ratio. Sell 60 shares to be delta neutral; gamma shows how fast that hedge drifts.

takeaways: Delta measures how much the option price moves for a $1 move in the stock.
Delta is a rough estimate of the chance of finishing in the money.
Delta times 100 gives the share-equivalent exposure of one contract.
Delta is the hedge ratio: sell that many shares to be delta neutral, for example over earnings.
caveats: Delta as probability is an approximation, not an exact figure.
The speaker's example strike is not given; $97 is an example value near 60 delta.
